written_before: any device arm of resfuse.py ran, and before elig_screen.py was run
question: c14-radical handed up 'residual accumulation on the pair tensor' at a band of 0.30-0.42 s and c14-byte-deletion closed NO-GO for a DIFFERENT variant of it (a producer writing into z's destination). The variant named in this row's brief is ttnn's own residual_input_tensor on layer_norm, which byte-deletion never tested. Does it collect the band, and is it eligible at the five pair residuals at all?

two_variants_kept_apart.V1_producer_destination: the block's last op writes its update straight into z. This is byte-deletion's C1. REFUTED THERE on firing: all five updates already come from L1, so the site costs read z + write z either way. Not re-run here.
two_variants_kept_apart.V2_residual_input_tensor: ttnn.layer_norm(x, residual_input_tensor=r) computes layer_norm(x + r) in one kernel, so the separate add_ disappears. This is what this row measures.

instrument_control: copy_ctl: ttnn.clone on the same [1,512,512,128] bf16 DRAM->DRAM tensor moves the same 2 Z. Known-answer: it must reproduce c14-byte-deletion's own measurement of this exact key on this exact node, 364.84 GB/s, within 340-390 GB/s. That window is an evidence-backed reproduction of a same-part same-key measurement, NOT the 380-460 GB/s roof window byte-deletion pre-registered and failed.

fold_conversion.rate_provenance: 423.6 GB/s is the add_ class's OWN in-fold rate, measured by c10-fold-census on qb2 at a during-sampled 1350 MHz. Borrowed for the pass->seconds conversion only, which is why every fold number here is a band and not a book entry.
fold_conversion.derivation: today an eligible site costs 4 pair passes: add_ reads z and rewrites z (the update is already in L1, so it is free), then the consuming norm reads z and writes z_norm. Fused it costs 2: the norm reads z, takes the update from L1, writes z_norm. 2 passes x 0.0418 s = 0.0836 s per eligible site per fold.
fold_conversion.all_five_eligible_would_be: 5 sites x 2 passes x 0.0418 s = 0.418 s, which reproduces the top of c14-radical's 0.30-0.42 s band. So the band is exactly the claim 'all five residuals are eligible'.
fold_conversion.mass_filter: 0.3 s needs 7.2 deleted passes per layer = 3.6 eligible sites, so 4 of the 5 residuals must be eligible for this to clear the filter at all.

eligible_pair_sized_sites_per_Pairformer.reasoning: ttnn.layer_norm returns ONE tensor, the normed output; the sum x+r is never materialised (checked in the 0.67.4 docstring: 'Returns: ttnn.Tensor: the output tensor'). tt_bio/eltwise_fusion.py:97 states the same contract: valid only where the add's result feeds nothing but the norm. At every one of the five pair residuals the sum has TWO consumers by construction -- the next block's input norm, and the next ttnn.add_ which takes z as its in-place accumulator target. A residual stream cannot have a single-consumer sum.
eligible_pair_sized_sites_per_Pairformer.positive_branch: >= 4 of 5 eligible, which is the only way the 0.3 s filter is reachable

fused_over_shipped_ratio.reasoning: fused_l1 deletes the whole add_ op. If the add_ is byte-bound at its measured 86.3 % of the stream roof, dropping 2 of the site's 4 passes should return close to half. This arm is the mechanism's RATE and it is real; it is also NOT a correct rewrite, because it does not produce z.
fused_over_shipped_ratio.note: this arm is an upper bound on the mechanism and is reported as such, never as a lever

keep_over_shipped_ratio.reasoning: keep_l1 is the only rewrite that preserves the residual stream: fuse the norm AND still do the add_. Op count is unchanged and the pass count is unchanged (4 either way), so it should return nothing.
keep_over_shipped_ratio.positive_branch: <= 0.80 -- a real win from the fused kernel's better locality even with the add_ retained, which would reopen the band

what_would_make_it_negative: copy_ctl outside 340-390 GB/s (instrument not reproducing byte-deletion's same-key figure, no arm believed), an A/A twin above 1.0 % (no arm separable at this size), fewer than 4 eligible sites (mechanism cannot reach the filter however fast it is), or keep_over_shipped >= 0.95 (the correct rewrite returns nothing).
verdict_rule: POSITIVE requires BOTH >= 4 eligible sites AND keep_over_shipped <= 0.80. Either one failing is a NO-GO, and a fast fused_l1 arm does not rescue it.
